title: ACP startup: a single transient stall aborts the turn (no retry), and the timeout error does not name the stalled step
body:
_This issue was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of @neubig._

## Summary

ACP startup (spawn → `initialize` → `authenticate` → `session/new` / `session/load`) runs under one aggregate hard deadline (`acp_startup_timeout`, default 90s) with no retry. If the ACP server stalls **once** during startup, the SDK aborts, the user's turn never starts, and the conversation goes to `ERROR`. A fresh launch right after the timeout starts at once, so a single retry would have saved the turn. The timeout error also does not say which startup step stalled.

The prompt path already retries transient failures (`_ACP_PROMPT_RETRY_DELAYS`, `_RETRIABLE_CONNECTION_ERRORS`, `-32603`). The startup path has no equivalent.

## Impact

What the user sees (from the code and the repro below):

- They send a message. After `acp_startup_timeout` seconds the conversation goes to `ERROR`, and the message is not processed. The ACP server never receives `session/prompt`.
- The error text is always `ACP startup timed out after Ns waiting for the ACP server to spawn, authenticate, and create/load a session`. The text is the same if the server hung in `initialize`, in `session/new`, in `session/load`, or in a model/mode call. Neither the user nor the logs show which step stalled or which ACP server it was.
- Through the agent server, the user gets **two** `ConversationErrorEvent`s for one failure: the typed `ACPStartupTimeout` (source `agent`) and a generic `TimeoutError` (source `environment`) from the run-loop backstop.
- To recover, the user has to send another message. That retry starts a fresh subprocess, which usually succeeds.

## Root cause

1. **One hard deadline around all of startup, and no retry.** `_start_acp_server` runs the whole `_init()` coroutine under `acp_startup_timeout`. When the deadline expires, it replaces the timeout with a generic message and re-raises:
   [`acp_agent.py#L3638-L3651`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L3638-L3651)
   ```python
   ) = self._executor.run_async(_init, timeout=self.acp_startup_timeout)
   except TimeoutError:
       raise TimeoutError(self._startup_timeout_message()) from None
   ```
   `_init()` covers the spawn ([L3312](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L3312)), `initialize` ([L3360](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L3360)), `authenticate`, `load_session` ([L3486](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L3486)) / `new_session` ([L3544](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L3544)), and the model, effort, and mode calls. Only `authenticate` has its own inner bound (`_ACP_AUTH_TIMEOUT`, 30s). Nothing around the call retries.
2. **The message has no phase.** [`_startup_timeout_message`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L3161-L3166) is a fixed string. It does not include the step in progress, the provider or command, or the subprocess stderr. Stderr is only logged line by line by `_log_acp_subprocess_stderr`.
3. **`init_state` surfaces the failure and re-raises.** [`acp_agent.py#L2536-L2570`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L2536-L2570) emits `ConversationErrorEvent(code=_classify_acp_init_error(e))`. Any `TimeoutError` maps to `ACPStartupTimeout` ([L1348-L1349](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L1348-L1349)), and the status goes to `ERROR`. `_agent_ready` stays `False` ([`local_conversation.py#L2048-L2072`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/impl/local_conversation.py#L2048-L2072)), so only the *next* `run()` tries startup again.
4. **The prompt path does retry.** [`acp_agent.py#L192-L195`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L192-L195) and [`#L4368-L4398`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/agent/acp_agent.py#L4368-L4398) retry `prompt()` on `OSError`/`ConnectionError`/`EOFError` and JSON-RPC `-32603`, with backoff. Startup has no equivalent, even for failures that happen before any server-side session exists.
5. **Duplicate error event in the agent server.** [`event_service.py#L1809-L1829`](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/blob/af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/event_service.py#L1809-L1829) publishes a backstop `ConversationErrorEvent(code=type(exc).__name__)` for every exception except `ConversationRunError`. `init_state` failures are not wrapped, so the backstop adds a second event after the typed one.

## Reproduction

The only stub is the external boundary: the ACP server subprocess. It is replaced by a ~30-line stdio JSON-RPC server that hangs on a chosen method on its first launch only, and behaves normally after that. All SDK code (`Conversation`, `ACPAgent.init_state`, `_start_acp_server`, the real subprocess and ACP connection) is real.

Save both files in one directory (for example `/tmp/acp_rca/`) and run from the repo root after `make build`:

```bash
uv run pytest /tmp/acp_rca/test_acp_startup_transient_stall.py -s -q -p no:cacheprovider -W ignore
```

`flaky_acp_server.py`:

```python
"""Minimal stdio ACP server. Stalls (never answers) the method named in
FLAKY_STALL_METHOD on the first launch only (every launch if FLAKY_STALL_ALWAYS
is set); other launches behave normally.
Every request method it receives is appended to FLAKY_LOG."""
import json, os, sys, time

marker, log = os.environ["FLAKY_MARKER"], os.environ["FLAKY_LOG"]
stall = os.environ.get("FLAKY_STALL_METHOD", "initialize")
first_launch = not os.path.exists(marker) or bool(os.environ.get("FLAKY_STALL_ALWAYS"))
open(marker, "a").close()

def send(msg):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msg) + "\n"); sys.stdout.flush()

for line in sys.stdin:
    msg = json.loads(line)
    if "id" not in msg:
        continue
    method, rid = msg["method"], msg["id"]
    with open(log, "a") as f:
        f.write(f"launch={'first' if first_launch else 'later'} {method}\n")
    if first_launch and method == stall:
        time.sleep(3600)
    if method == "initialize":
        send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {"protocolVersion": 1,
              "agentInfo": {"name": "flaky-acp", "version": "0.0.1"}}})
    elif method == "session/new":
        send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {"sessionId": "s1"}})
    elif method == "session/prompt":
        send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "session/update", "params": {
              "sessionId": "s1", "update": {"sessionUpdate": "agent_message_chunk",
              "content": {"type": "text", "text": "hello from the agent"}}}})
        send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {"stopReason": "end_turn"}})
    else:
        send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": rid, "result": {}})
```

`test_acp_startup_transient_stall.py` (the tests assert the **expected** behavior):

```python
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from openhands.sdk import Conversation
from openhands.sdk.agent import ACPAgent
from openhands.sdk.event.conversation_error import ConversationErrorEvent

SERVER = str(Path(__file__).with_name("flaky_acp_server.py"))


def _conversation(tmp_path, monkeypatch, stall_method, always=False):
    log = tmp_path / "requests.log"
    monkeypatch.setenv("FLAKY_MARKER", str(tmp_path / "launched"))
    monkeypatch.setenv("FLAKY_LOG", str(log))
    monkeypatch.setenv("FLAKY_STALL_METHOD", stall_method)
    if always:
        monkeypatch.setenv("FLAKY_STALL_ALWAYS", "1")
    events: list = []
    conv = Conversation(
        agent=ACPAgent(acp_command=[sys.executable, SERVER], acp_startup_timeout=3),
        workspace=str(tmp_path),
        persistence_dir=str(tmp_path / "conv"),
        callbacks=[events.append],
        visualizer=None,
    )
    conv.send_message("say hello")
    return conv, events, log


def test_transient_pre_session_stall_is_retried_and_turn_starts(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    conv, events, log = _conversation(tmp_path, monkeypatch, "initialize")
    try:
        conv.run()  # the server stalls once on `initialize`, then is healthy
    finally:
        print("\nrequests seen by the ACP server:\n" + log.read_text())
        print("errors:", [(e.code, e.detail) for e in events
                          if isinstance(e, ConversationErrorEvent)])
    requests = log.read_text().splitlines()
    assert sum(r.endswith("session/new") for r in requests) == 1
    assert sum(r.endswith("session/prompt") for r in requests) == 1


def test_startup_timeout_names_the_stalled_phase(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    conv, events, log = _conversation(tmp_path, monkeypatch, "session/new", always=True)
    with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):
        conv.run()
    [error] = [e for e in events if isinstance(e, ConversationErrorEvent)]
    print("\nerror:", error.code, repr(error.detail))
    assert error.code == "ACPStartupTimeout"
    assert "session/new" in error.detail


def test_permanent_stall_still_terminates(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    conv, events, log = _conversation(tmp_path, monkeypatch, "initialize", always=True)
    start = time.monotonic()
    with pytest.raises(TimeoutError):
        conv.run()
    assert time.monotonic() - start < 30
    assert [e.code for e in events if isinstance(e, ConversationErrorEvent)] == [
        "ACPStartupTimeout"
    ]
```

Observed on `main` at `af85e224c9c0698e2b34efac4c27d254c64b151b`:

```
requests seen by the ACP server:
launch=first initialize
errors: [('ACPStartupTimeout', 'ACP startup timed out after 3s waiting for the ACP server to spawn, authenticate, and create/load a session')]
F
error: ACPStartupTimeout 'ACP startup timed out after 3s waiting for the ACP server to spawn, authenticate, and create/load a session'
F.
E           TimeoutError: ACP startup timed out after 3s waiting for the ACP server to spawn, authenticate, and create/load a session
E       AssertionError: assert 'session/new' in 'ACP startup timed out after 3s waiting for the ACP server to spawn, authenticate, and create/load a session'
FAILED test_acp_startup_transient_stall.py::test_transient_pre_session_stall_is_retried_and_turn_starts
FAILED test_acp_startup_transient_stall.py::test_startup_timeout_names_the_stalled_phase
2 failed, 1 passed
```

(`test_permanent_stall_still_terminates` passes on `main`. It guards that a fix keeps a permanent stall bounded.)

The same scenario through a real local agent server (`uv run python -m openhands.agent_server`, started with the `FLAKY_*` env vars, then `POST /api/conversations` with `agent_settings={"agent_kind":"acp","acp_server":"custom","acp_command":[<python>, "flaky_acp_server.py"],"acp_startup_timeout":5}` and `initial_message.run=true`):

```
status after first message: error
ConversationErrorEvent agent       ACPStartupTimeout ACP startup timed out after 5s waiting for the ACP server to spawn, authenticate, and create/load a session
ConversationErrorEvent environment TimeoutError      ACP startup timed out after 5s waiting for the ACP server to spawn, authenticate, and create/load a session
requests seen by server: launch=first initialize
-- POST /events (second user message, run=true)
status: running -> finished
requests seen by server: launch=later initialize, launch=later session/new, launch=later session/prompt, ...
```

## Expected behavior

- A stall or transport drop **before a session exists** (spawn, `initialize`, a non-interactive `authenticate`) is retried once with a fresh subprocess. The first user turn then starts, and exactly one session is created.
- A permanent stall still ends in a bounded time with `ACPStartupTimeout`.
- The timeout error names the stalled step (for example `initialize`, `session/new`, `session/load`) and the ACP server (provider key or command basename). If stderr is available, it includes a short redacted tail.
- One startup failure produces one `ConversationErrorEvent`.

## Suggested fix

1. In `_start_acp_server`, track the current step in a local variable (`spawn` / `initialize` / `authenticate` / `session/new` / `session/load` / `set_model` / `set_mode`). Use it in `_startup_timeout_message()`, together with `self.acp_server` or `basename(acp_command[0])`.
2. Retry once only for failures before `session/new` / `session/load` was sent: a timeout in `initialize`, a timeout in a non-interactive `authenticate`, or `ConnectionError`/`EOFError` before the `initialize` response. Before the retry, tear down the subprocess and connection with the existing `_cleanup()` path. Do not retry after `session/new`/`session/load` was sent, so no duplicate provider sessions are created, and do not retry `ACPFileCredentialNeedsReauthError`/auth errors. Keep the total time bounded: give each attempt its own `acp_startup_timeout`, or split one budget, and document which.
3. In `EventService._run_and_publish`, skip the backstop `ConversationErrorEvent` when `init_state` already emitted a typed one. For example, wrap the `init_state` failure in `ConversationRunError`, or mark the exception.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With an ACP server that stalls once in `initialize`, `conversation.run()` succeeds on the first call, the server gets exactly one `session/new` and one `session/prompt`, and a warning about the retry is logged.
- [ ] With an ACP server that always stalls, `run()` still raises `TimeoutError` within a documented bound and emits exactly one `ACPStartupTimeout` event.
- [ ] The `ACPStartupTimeout` detail names the stalled step and the ACP server.
- [ ] No retry happens after `session/new`/`session/load` was sent, or for auth/re-auth errors (covered by a test).
- [ ] Through the agent server, an ACP startup failure produces exactly one `ConversationErrorEvent`.

## OpenHands AI triage
**The following comments and acceptance criteria were added by the OpenHands AI agent.**

### Triage
Verified against `main` at `af85e22`: `_start_acp_server()` runs the whole `_init()` coroutine (spawn, `initialize`, `authenticate`, `session/new`/`session/load`, model/effort/mode calls) under a single `acp_startup_timeout` and converts the deadline into a fixed, phase-less message; `init_state()` emits the typed `ConversationErrorEvent` and re-raises, leaving `_agent_ready` false so only the next `run()` retries startup; and `EventService._run_and_publish()` publishes its backstop `ConversationErrorEvent(source="environment")` for any exception that is not a `ConversationRunError`, adding a second event for cold-start failures. The prompt path already retries `_RETRIABLE_CONNECTION_ERRORS` and `-32603`; startup has no equivalent.

Scope: (1) one automatic retry with a fresh subprocess for transient startup failures that occur before a session is created — a startup deadline expiry in spawn/`initialize`/non-interactive `authenticate`, or `ConnectionError`/`EOFError`-class transport drops before the `initialize` response — using the existing `_cleanup()` teardown path between attempts; (2) the `ACPStartupTimeout` detail names the stalled startup step and the ACP server (provider key or command basename); (3) exactly one `ConversationErrorEvent` per startup failure through the agent server, reusing the existing `ConversationRunError` skip mechanism in `_run_and_publish()`; (4) total startup time stays bounded and the bound is documented in the code.

Non-goals: no retry after `session/new`/`session/load` was sent (no duplicate provider sessions); no retry for auth-classified failures (`ACPAuthRequired`, `ACPFileCredentialNeedsReauthError`); no configurable retry count or backoff policy; no changes to the prompt-path retry behavior; no subprocess stderr tail added to the error detail (stderr is already logged by `_log_acp_subprocess_stderr`, and this avoids widening the redaction surface).

The issue's own repro (flaky stdio ACP server stub, real SDK everywhere else) matches the repo's existing test technique for ACP startup timeouts (`tests/sdk/agent/test_acp_agent.py::test_start_acp_server_bounds_a_hung_handshake_call`, `test_init_state_surfaces_startup_timeout`) and is sufficient observable validation.

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] With an ACP server that stalls once before session creation (e.g. hangs on `initialize`, healthy on the next launch), a single `run()` call succeeds without raising; the ACP server log shows exactly one `session/new` (or `session/load`) followed by `session/prompt`; and a warning-level log naming the retry is emitted.
- [ ] Before the second spawn, the first attempt's ACP subprocess is terminated and its connection is closed via the existing `_cleanup()` path (observable: the first attempt's process is no longer alive after the retry completes, and the server log records a second launch).
- [ ] With an ACP server that stalls on every launch before session creation, `run()` still raises `TimeoutError` within a documented bound (each attempt bounded by `acp_startup_timeout`, stated in code), and exactly one `ConversationErrorEvent` with code `ACPStartupTimeout` is emitted.
- [ ] The `ACPStartupTimeout` event detail names the stalled startup step (e.g. `initialize`, `authenticate`, `session/new`, `session/load`) and the ACP server identity (provider key or command basename); a test asserts the step name appears for a server stalled at a known step.
- [ ] A startup failure raised after `session/new`/`session/load` was sent triggers no second subprocess spawn and no second session request (covered by a test), and auth-classified failures (`ACPAuthRequired`, `ACPFileCredentialNeedsReauthError`) are not retried (covered by a test).
- [ ] Through a local agent server, an ACP startup failure produces exactly one `ConversationErrorEvent` for the failure and the conversation status ends as `ERROR`.
